narrative.overview: The Mini App is read, not operated like a control panel. Its reading surface behaves like a printed column: a head line that says what you are looking at and how fresh it is, a packed strip of counters divided by rules, then entries separated by hairlines. No cards, no tiles, no shadows. The operator opens it between meetings, glances down one vertical rhythm, and closes it.
keyCharacteristics: Hairline rules as the only separator; no borders wrapped around content, no cards.
One accent, used for new records and the active filter.
Six type steps with tracked caps labels.
Numbers are tabular; the column head is the only thing that animates on a range switch.
Controls keep a 6px radius; sheets get 14px; entries get none.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: The accent marks the new and the selected. Any other use is decoration and gets removed.

rules.name: The Client Ground Rule
rules.body: Background, ink and primary come from themeParams; a hardcoded brand surface is a bug, not a preference.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every number that lines up in a column uses tabular figures.

rules.name: The Caps Label Rule
rules.body: A label is 11px, 600, uppercase, 0.14em. If it needs to be bigger to be read, it is a heading, not a label.

rules.name: The Flow Is Flat Rule
rules.body: If it scrolls with the page it is flat: rule, background, or nothing. Shadows are for surfaces that cover other content.

dos: Do separate with a single 1px rule; a second weight or a double border is undefined.
Do keep the reading column edge-to-edge and square.
Do put the count and the timestamp in the column head, not in the entries.
Do use tabular figures and nowrap for counters so a value change cannot reflow.
Do state a mode twice when it matters: the access switch is drawn and the mode is written beside it.
donts: Don't put cards in a reading flow, or wrap a list in a card that wraps another.
Don't give an in-flow surface a shadow, a gradient, or a coloured left border.
Don't introduce a second accent; the mark is the only colour that does a job.
Don't use emoji or font glyphs as icons.
Don't ship the dashboard vocabulary: hero metrics, coloured stat tiles, sparklines.
